title: Eight assertions for constructible prime coefficients on reduced proper curves
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], let $r$ be a prime number, and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $R$-modules on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$, where $R=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Then all eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] hold for the cohomology of its underlying abelian sheaf: (C1) vanishing in degrees $q>2$; (C2) vanishing for $q>1$ if $C$ is affine; (C3) vanishing for $q>1$ if $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $F$ is $p$-primary; (C4) finiteness in every degree if $F$ is constructible and has torsion prime to the characteristic; (C5) finiteness in every degree if $f$ is proper and $F$ is constructible; (C6) bijectivity of the cohomology pullback map in every degree and every cartesian square over an algebraically closed field extension if $F$ has torsion prime to the characteristic; (C7) the same bijectivity if $f$ is proper; (C8) surjectivity of the cohomology restriction in degree two for every open immersion into $C$.

proof.text: Zero-dimensional schemes (Stacks, proof of Lemma 0A5B, first paragraph: higher etale cohomology of any sheaf on a point vanishes). Let $Z$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $\le0$ and $G$ a torsion sheaf on $Z_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology], $H^q(Z,G)=0$ for $q>0$ and $H^0(Z,G)=\prod_{z\in|Z|}G_{\bar z}$, a finite product; this gives (C1), (C2), (C3) (all groups in degrees $\ge2$ vanish), and (C4), (C5): if $G$ is constructible its restriction to each stratum of a finite partition is locally constant with finite stalks, so each $G_{\bar z}$ is finite. Every open $U\subseteq Z$ is again of dimension $\le0$, so $H^2(U,G|_U)=0$ and the restriction in (C8) is surjective. (C6) and (C7) are [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-field-extension]. Hence $\mathcal C(Z,G)$ holds [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Lemma 0A5B (lemma-constant-smooth-statements), first paragraph

proof.text: Smooth constant coefficients and extension by zero (Stacks 03SG, lemma-even-easier, and 0A5B, lemma-constant-smooth-statements). Let X be smooth, separated and of finite type over the algebraically closed k, with dimension at most one. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Its local rings are normal domains by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. Two distinct irreducible components cannot meet: at an intersection the local ring would have two distinct minimal primes, contrary to being a domain. Thus the components are pairwise disjoint; each is open because its complement is the finite union of the other closed components. Write their inclusions as i_a:X_a -> X, which are closed immersions and hence finite. For a prime r, if r is nonzero in k, apply [lemma-weil-pbc-smooth-curve-kummer-localization] to each X_a; otherwise k has characteristic r and apply [lemma-weil-pbc-smooth-curve-artin-schreier]. These statements supply all eight assertions for the constant prime-field sheaf, including for points; their smooth-curve calculations follow [thm-sc-main]. For an open j:U -> X, put U_a = U intersect X_a. If U_a is empty, its extension by zero is zero and all assertions hold. Otherwise U_a is dense in the irreducible X_a; apply [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-dense-open] to its constant sheaf, which is constructible and killed by r. This gives the assertions for extension by zero from U_a. Their finite pushforwards along i_a satisfy the assertions by [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-finite-pushforward]. The stalk formula for [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] identifies j_! of the constant sheaf with the finite direct sum of these pushforwards. Split short exact sequences and [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] assemble the sum. Zero-dimensional pieces also follow from step 1.

Locally constant coefficients on an irreducible open, trace reduction (Stacks Lemma 03SD, first paragraph). Let $X$ be a reduced separated finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim X\le1$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion with $U$ irreducible, $\ell$ a prime and $G$ a finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on $U$; we prove $\mathcal C(X,j_!G)$ in this and the next three steps. By [lemma-weil-pbc-curve-locally-constant-reduction] there is a connected finite etale $v:V\to U$ of degree prime to $\ell$ such that $v^{-1}G$ has a finite filtration with quotients $\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}_V$, and the unit and trace $G\xrightarrow{\eta}v_*v^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{tr}}G$ compose to $\deg(v)\cdot\mathrm{id}_G$, an automorphism since $\ell\nmid\deg v$ and $\ell G=0$. Applying the additive functor $j_!$, the maps $a=j_!\eta:j_!G\to H:=j_!v_*v^{-1}G$ and $b=j_!\operatorname{tr}$ satisfy $b\circ a=\deg(v)\,\mathrm{id}$. Both sheaves are killed by $\ell$, so each is torsion prime to $p=\operatorname{char}k$ if $\ell\neq p$ and $p$-primary if $\ell=p$ [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]; and $H$ is constructible: $v^{-1}G$ is finite locally constant on the Noetherian $V$ (one stratum), $v_*v^{-1}G$ is constructible on $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-constructible-noetherian] ($v$ is finite), and its extension by zero is constructible on $X$ (the strata of $U$ together with the closed complement $X\setminus U$, on which it is $0$) [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-retract] it suffices to prove $\mathcal C(X,j_!v_*v^{-1}G)$.

proof.text: Compactifying $V$ over $X$ (Stacks Lemma 03SD, Zariski's main theorem). The composite $j\circ v:V\to X$ is quasi-finite (finite etale followed by an open immersion), separated (finite morphisms and immersions are separated) and of finite type, and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Noetherian). By [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] it factors as $V\xrightarrow{j_0}T\xrightarrow{p}X$ with $j_0$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ finite. Let $Y\subseteq T$ be the closure of $j_0(V)$ with its reduced induced structure; $Y$ is closed in $T$, so $\bar f=p|_Y:Y\to X$ is finite, and $Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $\le\dim X\le1$ (finite morphisms are integral, so they do not raise dimension). $V$ is reduced (etale over the reduced $U$), so $j_0$ factors through an open immersion $j':V\hookrightarrow Y$ with dense image, and $\bar f\circ j'=j\circ v$. The square with sides $j',v,\bar f,j$ is cartesian: $j'(V)\subseteq\bar f^{-1}(U)$ is open; the $U$-morphism $V\to\bar f^{-1}(U)$ goes from a finite $U$-scheme to a separated $U$-scheme, so it is finite, in particular closed; its image is open, closed and dense in $\bar f^{-1}(U)$, hence all of it, and as both are reduced open subschemes of $Y$ with the same underlying set, $V=U\times_XY$. The dimension bound follows on affine charts from [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability]: a strict chain of primes in a finite algebra contracts to a strict chain in the base. Reduced closure means the radical of the closed-image ideal; on V that ideal is zero because V is reduced. Thus the inclusion of V remains an open immersion after this replacement. Finiteness of V -> inverse-image(U) uses [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated], and closedness uses [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Since this inclusion is both open and closed and dense, its image is the whole inverse image. A surjective open immersion is an isomorphism, proving the cartesian assertion without identifying schemes merely by their underlying sets.

proof.text: Exchange of $j_!$ and finite direct image (Stacks Lemma 0GJ1, as used in 03SD). For the cartesian square of step 5 (open immersions $j'$, $j$; $\bar f$ finite; $v$ its base change), [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] says that the comparison morphism $\beta:j_!v_*E\to\bar f_*j'_!E$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison] is an isomorphism for every abelian sheaf $E$ on $V_{\Et}$. With $E=v^{-1}G$ this gives $j_!v_*v^{-1}G\cong\bar f_*j'_!v^{-1}G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-curve-assertions-finite-pushforward] for the finite $\bar f:Y\to X$, it suffices to prove $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!v^{-1}G)$.

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Lemma 03SD, third paragraph; Lemma 0GJ1 (lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite)

proof.text: Filtration and reduction to the constant sheaf (Stacks Lemma 03SD, end). Let $0=E_0\subset E_1\subset\cdots\subset E_m=v^{-1}G$ be the filtration of step 4, with $E_i/E_{i-1}\cong\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}_V$. Since $j'_!$ is exact [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], $0=j'_!E_0\subset\cdots\subset j'_!E_m=j'_!v^{-1}G$ is a filtration with quotients $j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}$, i.e. there are short exact sequences $0\to j'_!E_{i-1}\to j'_!E_i\to j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell}\to0$. Step 3, applied to the reduced curve $Y$ and the open immersion $j'$, gives $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell})$, and induction on $i$ with [lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage] gives $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!E_i)$ for all $i$, in particular $\mathcal C(Y,j'_!v^{-1}G)$. By steps 6 and 4, $\mathcal C(X,j_!G)$ holds.

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Lemma 03SD, last paragraph; Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements)

proof.text: Constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-coefficients on a reduced curve (Stacks Theorem 03SC, proof, third and fourth paragraphs). Let $X$ be a reduced separated finite-type $k$-scheme with $\dim X\le1$, $\ell$ a prime and $G$ a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on $X_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-curve-dense-open-localization] there is a dense open $U=\coprod_aU_a\subseteq X$, a finite disjoint union of irreducible open subschemes $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X$, on which $G$ is finite locally constant, such that $\mathcal C(X,G)$ holds if and only if $\mathcal C(X,j_{a,!}(G|_{U_a}))$ holds for every $a$. Each $G|_{U_a}$ is a finite locally constant sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces on the irreducible $U_a$, so steps 4 to 7 give $\mathcal C(X,j_{a,!}(G|_{U_a}))$. Hence $\mathcal C(X,G)$ holds; in particular, when $X$ is proper over $k$, its seventh conjunct $\mathcal C_7(X,G)$ [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] holds.

source.place: Section 03SB, proof of Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), third and fourth paragraphs

proof.text: Coefficient bookkeeping. Put R = ULift(F_r). In every R-module stalk multiplication by r is zero because r = 0 in R, so the underlying abelian sheaf is torsion. The finite coefficient field is Noetherian, as required by short-exact devissage. The prime-field module structure is uniquely determined by the abelian group, and [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion-modules-agree] identifies the finite-stalk constructible stratifications used above with constructibility as modules. Forgetting modules to abelian groups preserves the local trivializations, inverse image, finite direct image and extension by zero: the latter two are respectively finite products on stalks and the original stalk or zero. Hence the eight assertions in step 8 are exactly IsCurve.Assertions R f F, whose cohomology and all comparison maps are defined on the underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. This proves the assertion package without selecting only C7.
